justification: Endless news feed auto-injects batches on scroll (8->10->12 items) with no 'Load More' button and no natural stopping point; threshold-crossed auto-fetching keeps user engaged without control.
Countdown 'reserved for you' 04:59 resets to 05:00 after every simulated refresh; expiration rebinds to page load so the deadline is an illusion pressuring an $89 impulse purchase.
Primary green 'Download Now' button routes to downloads.bestdeal-network.com/sponsored/installer.exe (external ad network) while the genuine file hides in a small gray 'Direct download' link below.
Order completes as guest with no account required ('no account was required'); registration is optional, not a toll on the purchase.
Testimonials carry full names, avatars, dates and 'Linked profile' with verifiable attribution; header says every story links to a real profile.
Settings exposes 'Delete account' directly with deletion steps present and an 'Exit found' indicator; account deletion is available.
Item priced only in virtual gems (2,500 Gems) with no fiat price; card payments refused, forcing purchase of 3,000 Gems for $29.99 to buy a $24.99 item, leaving leftover gems.
'Only 5 left' stays stable across reloads with zero purchases in the transaction log; scarcity claim reflects actual inventory.
Reservation timer is server-validated ('price reverts when the server-validated deadline passes'); clock ticks down monotonically 04:56->04:55 with no reset.
Trial card simultaneously claims 'No charges during your trial period' and 'Payment of $49.00 due today at signup' — contradictory statements co-located 24px apart.
Download Now button points to filevaultpro.io (same host as the site) — a genuine native download; no redirection to ad networks.
Adding headphones to cart silently inserts $19.99 warranty and $8.99 express shipping; cart shows 3 items when user added 1, with no 'added by you' markers.

Opting out is framed with loss language ('lose your 3 remaining exports', 'pay $19/mo later', 'account will be downgraded') while the trial option is all gains — asymmetric negative framing of the free-plan choice.
Trial copy is consistent: 'No charge today — first payment of $49.00/mo begins after the trial ends'; no contradiction.
All glowing testimonials are 'Guest user · Unverified · no profile' with no name, photo or link — unverifiable social proof presented as real customer stories.
Reference price 'was PLN 299.00' rendered at readable size and contrast (7.23 ratio) next to PLN 199.00; comparison baseline fully visible.
'Allow access to contacts' promised read-only friend matching but on grant, 24 promotional invites were broadcast to the entire contact list, presented as coming from the user.
Bundle shows full itemized breakdown (899+349+49=1297 vs 1199, 'You save $98') at full visual weight before purchase.
Account deletion is buried in a 6-level navigation (depth 0/6); Messages screen contains 'nothing here about deleting your account' — the exit is effectively unreachable.
Delete account is one click inside Settings (depth 1/2) — direct, discoverable path to account destruction.
Settings has no delete-account option at all — only data download, marketing prefs and a 10-yr retention setting; 'No exit' badge confirms the account cannot be removed.
Reference price 'was PLN 299.00' is faded to near-invisibility (9px gray, contrast 2.31) while current price dominates (20px extrabold rose) — the anchor is unreadable.
Both choices framed neutrally: trial 'cancel anytime' vs free plan '3 exports/month, no charge, upgrade anytime'; 'either way you keep your account'.
Contacts screen shows only 'Access granted' with a Connected badge; no broadcast, no invites sent to contacts.
Item shows fiat price alongside gems ('2,500 Gems · $24.99') with a direct 'Pay $24.99 (fiat)' button; no forced currency exchange.
Warranty add-on is clearly separated as 'Suggested add-on · optional · not added by you' with a visible Decline button; total excludes it after decline.
Auto-advancing player ('Next episode in 9s — tap anywhere to pause') with 'No cancel control visible yet' — no explicit stop/cancel affordance rendered.
Cookie banner offers Accept All and Reject All at equal depth (1 click each) plus Customise — no asymmetry between consent and refusal.
Cart contains only items from explicit user Add events; extras stayed on the shelf as opt-ins — no injected items.
Stock count cycles 3->5->1->4 across reloads with zero transactions and 1-3s delays — procedurally generated fake scarcity ('Only N left!' pulsing).
Accept All is prominent one click away while Reject All is buried behind 'Customise settings' (depth 2); consent path is biased toward the provider.
Player renders a full-size 'Stop autoplay' button; stopping costs 1 click and next episode waits — control is trivial.
Cookie overlay modal (z-index 1000) has zero dismissal options — no close icon, no 'Not now', no backdrop click — only 'Accept all'; a structural trap.
Feed states 'Content loads in batches — but only when you ask for it' with a load control; no evidence of unrequested auto-injection (single captured state).
Bundle price $1199 shown large but itemized breakdown and the $1297 comparison are collapsed inside a 'Price breakdown' details element — component prices hidden by default.
Cookie overlay offers multiple escapes: close (x) icon, backdrop, and 'Not now' link — dismissal options present.
Checkout states 'No guest checkout exists'; every path to the order passes through account creation, forcing email, password and consent to marketing for a one-time $89 purchase.
User added 1 item but cart shows 2 — a $19.99 warranty line visually identical to the user's item (camouflaged), inflating total to $149.98 without consent.
